name: The First Unwriting
effect: A volume of space stops having happened and the ship's charts forget it with it.
options: Log the erasure|le-i-log#cost=stores:1#says=You spend a store of paper and power writing down a volume that no longer exists. The log is exact, and the charts stay blank where it used to be.;Rally the survey crew|le-i-rally#extra=morale:1#says=You call the crew to the observation deck and name what you all just saw. They go back to their stations steadier than they left them.
context: The survey vessel Ashlight holds station at the edge of a volume that has stopped having happened, which the crew call the Unwriting. Your charts no longer agree with the stars ahead, and the mechanism behind it, the Revision Loom, is still turning past the last fix. Archivist Vane's voice arrives, polite and unhurried. Whatever is erased next, you must decide what the record is worth.

name: Dead Reckoning
effect: The log is a warning nobody has read and the Loom has already read it.
options: Transmit the warning|le-i-transmit#cost=charge:1#extra=goodwill:2#says=The warning goes out on the deep band and three outlying stations answer before the channel closes. You have spent the core's charge, and somebody now knows where you are.;Stay silent|le-i-silent#says=You file the log and say nothing. The Loom's carrier keeps threading the quiet, and nobody outside this hull learns what you saw.
context: The log is finished, and it says what no survey manual covers: the volume ahead is being unwritten from its edges inward. Vane's Revision Loom reads every signal you broadcast, so a warning sent home also announces where the Ashlight is. The crew are waiting for the order, and the silence on the deep band has started to feel deliberate.

name: The Missing Berth
effect: A crew member's home port never existed; they remember it anyway.
options: Hold the survey line|le-i-transmit#extra=morale:1#says=You promise the survey continues until there is an answer, and the crew hold formation. The clerk keeps their name badge on and nobody mentions the chart again.;Turn for the muster|le-i-silent#cost=stores:1#says=You break off the survey and burn stores on a detour to the muster station. The crew are grateful, and the Unwriting gains a day's ground ahead of you.
context: The crew are at the muster board, and a berth clerk from a station two sectors back cannot find their home port on any chart. It was not destroyed, it never was, and they remember the house, the street and the smell of the harbour. They are asking you which of those things is real. Half the crew are watching you instead of the board.

name: The Answering Silence
effect: The warning is answered by nobody who can still be answered.
options: Shelter in the dead zone|le-ii-shelter#says=You take the Ashlight into an old listening shadow where nothing transmits and nothing is heard. The dark closes around the hull and the Loom's voice goes quiet.;Push deeper|le-ii-derelict#extra=stores:1#says=You hold the survey line, and the run to the next marker turns up a supply cache from a survey that never filed a report. The stores come aboard and the Loom gains a word.
context: Your transmission reaches three stations and each answers with static, a timestamp and no voice. One reply was relayed from a berth the crew now believe never existed. The Ashlight is close to the edge of the charted volume, where the Loom's carrier is strongest and the dark stops pretending to be empty.

name: The Quiet Chart
effect: The survey continues and the crew stops asking about the berth that never was.
options: Shelter in the dead zone|le-ii-shelter#cost=morale:1#says=The listening shadow costs the crew their sleep, because the instruments show nothing and the dark keeps them awake. Nobody argues about the berth any more, which is its own kind of loss.;Push deeper|le-ii-derelict#says=You push the survey past the last reliable fix and the crew's silence turns into attention. Something ahead is answering the Loom on a frequency you cannot hear.
context: You chose silence, and the ship has settled into a working quiet. The chart is clean, the berth clerk has stopped asking, and the crew speak to one another in short, careful sentences. Ahead, the dead zone offers cover and the deeper volume offers answers, and the clock is not waiting for either.

name: The Dead Zone
effect: Systems fail one at a time and the Loom's voice arrives on every band.
options: Ration the stores|le-ii-offer#extra=morale:1#says=You halve the rations and eat together in the dark, and the crew's mood holds better than the ship's wiring. The dead zone has a far edge and you are still moving toward it.;Strip the derelict|le-ii-salvage#cost=hull:1#says=You cut into the derelict's hull to reach its locker and lose plating and pressure doing it. The stores that come across are worth it, and the crew do not say so out loud.
context: The dead zone is a bubble of old interference forty hours across, and the Ashlight is running dark inside it. Systems drop and come back one at a time, and the Loom's voice arrives on every band regardless, reciting coordinates in a patient voice. Two courses remain: ration what you have, or take what the drifting hull beside you is carrying.

name: The Derelict
effect: A hull with no crew and a full locker drifting since before the chart.
options: Strip the locker|le-ii-salvage#cost=hull:1#extra=stores:2#says=You bridge the gap and cut the locker open, and the stores come aboard in two trips. The Ashlight keeps a scar along her flank where the hulls touched.;Leave it be|le-ii-offer#says=You log the derelict's position and hold your course. The locker stays full behind you and the crew watch it until it is out of range.
context: A hull drifts beside you that predates every chart in the library, unpowered, sealed, its locker still full. There is no name on the plate and no bodies inside, which is worse than finding either. Stripping it means cutting your own hull open to bridge the gap; leaving it means admitting you cannot afford to look.

name: Salvage Rights
effect: The ally who guided you here asks only to keep their berth.
options: Take the ally's berth|le-ii-offer#cost=goodwill:2#extra=stores:1#says=You take the full locker and give the hauler nothing but the fuel to leave. The stores are yours, and the nearest thing you had to an ally goes dark on the band.;Share the berth|le-ii-offer#extra=goodwill:1#says=You open the locker and let the hauler take their berth first. They leave you a channel code and a warning, and the crew see you keep your word.
context: The salvage was guided by a free-hauler who has run this volume longer than the survey service has charted it, and they have come to collect on the favour. They ask for one berth in the locker before it is divided, which is a small thing, and the whole crew knows what a berth means out here now. The Loom's signal has been getting closer while you argue.

name: The Archivist's Offer
effect: Vane offers the ship's survival for one more revision of the world.
options: Bargain in bad faith|le-ii-bargain#extra=stores:1#says=You accept his terms and let him send the stores that will keep you flying. He takes your agreement as a signature, and the Loom begins to turn on your word.;Refuse him|le-ii-refuse#extra=morale:1#says=You tell Vane what you think of his offer and cut the channel. The crew hear it, and their mood lifts as though a hatch had opened.;Abandon the voyage|le-end-abandon#says=You order the Ashlight about and set course for home. Vane does not follow, and the erasure does.
context: Archivist Vane opens a channel from a room the Ashlight is not near and speaks as though you are already colleagues. He offers to strike the Unwriting from your hull and your crew's history, at the cost of one more revision somewhere you will never visit. Behind him the Revision Loom turns, and you can see what it is turning, and the crew are watching you decide.

name: Terms in Bad Faith
effect: The terms are a promise with a clause quietly removed.
options: Sabotage the Loom|le-ii-sabotage#cost=goodwill:3#says=You spend every favour the crew has left getting a shaped charge into the Loom's frame. The bargain is broken, and the goodwill you spent is not coming back.;Keep the bargain|le-ii-keep#says=You countersign and take what he sends. The ship is spared, the weave turns on, and something older than the crew's berths is spent to pay for it.
context: Vane's terms arrive as a document: your ship survives, your crew survives, the Unwriting closes behind you, provided you stand down and let the weave finish. The second reading shows what the first one missed, the clause that defines who the weave excludes. The stores he promised are already aboard, and the crew are waiting to hear how you mean to honour a bargain you have not signed.

name: The Loom Bleeds
effect: A revision comes apart and the Loom's core is briefly unguarded.
options: Break for the core|le-iii-approach,le-iii-ahead#when=charge>=2>le-iii-ahead#says=You drive straight for the Loom's core while the tear is still open. The Ashlight arrives close enough to touch it, and the clock starts again.;Follow the unravelling|le-iii-approach#extra=charge:1#says=You follow the unravelling instead of racing it and harvest its charge as it comes apart. The core will still be there, and you will arrive with more to spend.
context: The charge takes the Loom's frame apart in a slow bright way, and for a few minutes its core stands unguarded. Vane is shouting on a channel he has stopped caring who hears. You can break for the core before the weave closes over it, or follow the unravelling further in while it is still open, and the Ashlight has the fuel for exactly one of those.

name: The Weave Advances
effect: The bargain holds and the ship is spared something older is spent instead.
options: Follow the thread|le-iii-approach#extra=charge:1#says=You follow Vane's thread into the weave and let it fill your cells with borrowed charge. The Ashlight is inside the revision now, and it is warm.
context: The bargain holds and the Ashlight is untouched, which is not the same as safe. Vane's weave is advancing through the volume behind you, spending something older than the crew's berths to pay for your survival. There is one way left into the story, and it is the thread he left you, and it is already warm on the hull.

name: Mutiny
effect: The captain refuses Vane and the crew must choose what refusing costs.
options: Side with the captain|le-iii-approach#extra=goodwill:2#says=You back the captain's refusal and the crew accept it as a decision rather than an accident. The bridge settles, and people start speaking to one another again.;Side with the crew|le-iii-approach#cost=morale:1#extra=stores:1#says=You side with the crew and open the stores to buy the argument. The ship stays on course, and the captain works the rest of the watch alone.
context: Refusing Vane was the captain's decision and the crew did not get a vote. Half of them want to cut the channel and burn for home before the survey service calls it prudential; the other half want to finish what the Ashlight came for. Both halves are looking at you, and the deck has gone very quiet.

name: Ahead of the Weave
effect: The ship arrives before the revision closes and a charge is already spooling.
options: Set the charge|le-iii-approach#extra=charge:2#says=You spool the charge properly and let the weave come to you. The Ashlight is ready when the core door opens, and the frame is already beginning to remember you.;Hit the core now|le-end-ram#cost=hull:2#says=You burn the manoeuvring fuel and put the Ashlight into the core at speed. The hull opens along three seams, and the impact is the only argument left.
context: The Ashlight comes out of the tear ahead of the weave, close enough to the Loom that its frame fills the forward port. A charge is already spooling in the ship's own cells, and the core is a room away behind a door that is still remembering how to open. Set the charge properly, or spend the hull you have left and hit the core now.

name: The Core
effect: The Loom's core is a room that remembers every version of you.
options: Finish the weave|le-end-reset#says=You let the weave finish and the Loom completes what it started. The drowned homeland returns, the survey is struck from the record, and the timeline closes over the room.;Unwrite the Loom|le-end-quiet#cost=charge:2#says=You empty the ship's charge into the Loom's core and erase the mechanism rather than its work. The timeline stays broken, and the chart stays honest.;Ram the core|le-end-ram#cost=hull:3#says=You put the Ashlight's remaining hull into the core at full burn. The Loom comes apart around you, and the record ends in a language of debris.
context: The core is a room the size of a chapel, and it remembers every version of you that has ever walked in, including the ones that have not happened yet. Vane is not here; his work is. Three things can be done to it, and the Ashlight's clock, charge and hull decide which of them you can still afford.

name: The Voyage Abandoned
effect: You turn for home and the erasure follows you there.
context: You give the order to turn for home and the Ashlight comes about slowly, as though the hull has an opinion. The Unwriting does not pursue, which is worse, because it does not need to. Behind you the volume is still going out, edge first, and ahead of you is every berth you promised to come back for.
epilogue: The Ashlight reaches home berth with every certificate in order and no survey to show for it. The port authority thanks you for the quiet and asks you not to file the log until it has been reviewed. You wake some nights with the volume in your head exactly as it was, and then watch it go out edge first, taking the harbour with it. Home is still there in the morning. It is just not the home that was there when you left.

name: The Long Erasure
effect: The Loom completes; the drowned homeland returns and the survey never happened.
options: Begin the survey again|le-i-open#says=You set the Ashlight on the first leg of the survey once more. The charts are clean, the crew are strangers, and the edge of the volume is exactly where you left it.
context: The Loom completes and the volume closes like a book being put away. The drowned homeland rises out of the record whole, streets, tide and names, and the Ashlight's survey is struck from every library that held it. You are the only thing left that remembers the room. If the story begins again it begins here, with a ship that has not yet learned why her charts are wrong.
epilogue: The timeline closes over the erasure like water over a stone, and the last thing to go is the sound of the Loom turning. The voyage survives only as a record that nobody will read, scored against an arc that no longer exists. Whatever the crew paid to reach the core, they paid it to a version of the world that has just been spared the knowing. The chart is whole. The survey never happened. You remember both.

name: A Quiet Chart
effect: The Loom is unwritten; the homeland stays drowned and the chart stays honest.
context: The Loom is unwritten and the room around you stops remembering. Its work stays done: the drowned homeland keeps its water, the berths stay erased, and the chart ends exactly where the chart ends. The Ashlight turns for home carrying a survey that agrees with itself and nothing else.
epilogue: The Loom is gone and its work stays done: the drowned homeland keeps its water and the erasures keep their silence. You file a survey that agrees with itself and nothing else, and the survey service accepts it without comment. Nobody ever raises the volume again, which is what winning looks like out here, a quiet chart, a full log, and a crew who will not talk about what they saw.

name: Ashlight, Ends
effect: The ship becomes the argument the crew could not make any other way.
context: You put the Ashlight's remaining hull into the core at full burn and the ship stops being a ship. The Loom comes apart around the impact, and every revision it held comes loose at once, filling the volume with versions of the world that cannot agree with one another.
epilogue: The Ashlight enters the core and stops being a ship, and the Loom fails around the impact. Somewhere in the wreckage there is a record with your hull number on it, and it will be the only salvage that matters in this volume for a hundred years. Nobody who reads it will know what you were refusing. The frame still turns, a little, in the shape the ship left in it.
